input.quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise
input.rationale: Section 18.9 is fully mutual and contains the M&A/successor carve-out: either Party (including Ono) may assign without the other's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise, subject only to an assumption writing. Other assignments require consent, and Affiliate assignments are permitted with consent that "shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed" — i.e., the rule's fallback consent standard, applied symmetrically to Array as well as to us. There is no Array right to terminate, re-price or otherwise exit on an Ono change of control: the only change-of-control provisions in the document (Section 18.10 and Section 4.5(b) at p0322) are triggered by a Change in Control of Array, not of Ono, and Section 18.10 imposes firewall obligations on Array's acquirer rather than granting any exit right. This sits at (and on the successor carve-out above) the fallback, so no redline. Noted but not flagged as deviations: the preferred position would allow Affiliate assignment without consent, and the proviso letting the non-assigning Party refuse consent where it reasonably believes an Affiliate assignment could cause it material adverse tax consequences is a narrow, reciprocal qualifier on a minor sub-element. We would also observe commercially (not as an assignment issue) that p0322 lets Array's Section 4.5(b) restrictions lapse on Array's own Change in Control, which is a separate non-compete point rather than a breach of this rule.
